title: Nomad performance kit: per-route + per-model observability canvas
creator: Mara Lin
description: Goal: Deliver a compact, interactive canvas for engineers to inspect per-route and per-model performance signals that balances density with actionable affordances. The Nomad performance kit focuses on four job stories: 1) triage latency spikes on a given route, 2) compare throughput and token-cost across model variants, 3) evaluate rollout canary health with lightweight statistical signals, and 4) jump from aggregate trends to token-level microtraces. This ticket contains the prototype spec, interaction notes, chart mapping, and review feedback for the first implementation slice.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas shows route-level latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and token throughput sparkline in a single row for chosen timeframe
Model variants are listed with quick compare bars for cost-per-token and mean latency, with an expandable detail pane
Canary/rollout panel allows toggling baseline vs canary with confidence band overlay and shows a pass/fail hint based on short-window p95 regression checks
Token-cost stack chart breaks down unit cost by batching, quantization, and kernel tier for the displayed period
Clicking a latency spike opens a token-level microtrace waterfall (KV cache hits, batch size, kernel fallback notes) and links to related GitHub PRs or incident runbooks
Prototype validated in design review with Eng and PM and no critical blocking UX issues remain
design_notes: Layout: horizontal lane per metric group to maintain scannability for SRE/ML engineers
Charts: use percentile ribbons rather than multiple lines to reduce clutter; ribbons should be selectable (hover highlights corresponding trace samples)
Interactivity: brushing on sparkline updates token-cost and microtrace panels; double-clicking a time bin zooms into 1-minute granularity
Accessibility: colorblind-friendly palette for ribbons and clear shape affordances for sparkline lines
Stateful comparisons: saved comparison presets (e.g., 'canary-v1.3 vs stable') persisted in user profile
Fallback: when model variant is unavailable, automatically show closest compatible variant and annotate in UI
chart_spec_map: latency_ribbon: percentile ribbon (p10-p90) with marker lines for p50/p95/p99; unit ms; aggregation: per-minute and rolling-1m
throughput_spark: per-second tokens/sec sparkline; color = route-tag; supports brush selection
token_cost_stack: stacked bar by cost component (batching, quant, kernel) with unit = USD/token; shows 7d/24h toggles
variant_compare_bars: horizontal bars showing mean latency and cost per token; click to expand into latency distribution histogram
microtrace_waterfall: waterfall view listing request phases (ingest, scheduling, kernel_exec, kv_lookup); annotates KV hit/miss and batch size
rollout_confidence: area chart overlay showing baseline/canary percentiles with a small-stat box (bayesian proportion test summary)
review_comments: PM (Leah Chen): add a quick action to pin a route to console home for on-call rotations
Eng (Ravi Patel): microtrace waterfall needs to surface KV cache version and kernel selection note for debugging regressions
SRE (Jonas Meyer): add an option to export the selected time window as a CSV for downstream analysis
Design (Aisha Kapoor): consider a condensed 'compact' mode for small laptop screens and embedding in runbooks
